title: Operator sees costs in the web console
description:
The console dashboard already shows job counts, the local-versus-batch worker
split, and average duration. Cost is the missing column: the worker breakdown
currently tells an operator that sixty percent of jobs ran locally without
telling them what the other forty percent cost.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Viewing costs in the web console

  Scenario: The dashboard shows cost alongside the worker split
    Given costs exist for the last thirty days
    When the operator opens the dashboard
    Then the total gpu cost is shown
    And the total avoided cost is shown

  Scenario: A cost page shows a daily breakdown
    Given costs exist for the last thirty days
    When the operator opens the costs page
    Then a daily cost series is shown

  Scenario: Costs can be scoped to a site
    Given costs exist for two sites
    When the operator filters the costs page by one site
    Then only that site's costs are shown

  Scenario: Reconciled days show estimate against actual
    Given a reconciled day exists
    When the operator opens the costs page
    Then that day shows both estimated and actual cost

  Scenario: An out of tolerance day is visibly flagged
    Given a reconciled day whose variance exceeds the threshold
    When the operator opens the costs page
    Then that day is flagged

  Scenario: The job detail page shows the job cost
    Given the operator is viewing a completed Batch job
    Then the job gpu cost and billed seconds are shown

  Scenario: A local job shows what it avoided
    Given the operator is viewing a completed local job
    Then the job gpu cost is zero
    And the job avoided cost is shown
```

## Implementation brief

**`console/lib/api.ts`** -- `fetchCosts(siteId?, from?, to?)` plus a
`CostSummary` / `DailyCost` interface. Extend `JobSummary` and `JobDetail`
with the cost attributes.

**`console/app/costs/page.tsx`** (new) -- summary tiles, a daily series, a
site filter, and an estimate-versus-actual comparison with the out-of-tolerance
flag. Wrap in `AuthGuard` like the other pages.

**`console/components/Header.tsx`** -- add the Costs nav entry.

**`console/app/page.tsx`** -- cost tiles beside the existing worker breakdown,
which is where the local-versus-batch split already lives and where cost makes
that split mean something.

**`console/app/jobs/detail/page.tsx`** -- cost in the execution telemetry card.

**Charting** -- if a chart library is introduced, check what `site/` already
uses before adding a dependency. A plain table is an acceptable first cut;
the numbers matter more than the visualisation.

**Do not repeat the fabricated-data pattern.** The job detail page currently
swallows fetch failures and renders a hardcoded mock job (auritus-69abb3, in
the M10 epic). Doing that with dollar figures would be considerably worse than
doing it with telemetry. Render loading, error, and empty states explicitly.

**Label estimates as estimates** in the UI, not only in the docs. A dollar
figure on a dashboard reads as authoritative unless it says otherwise.

## Blocked on

The daily cost rollups story, for `GET /admin/costs`.
